findings.title: Editing a shift description breaks its pending offers.
findings.scenario: Tom offers Sara one date, then edits only the shift description before Sara accepts. Saving replaces the existing dates and detaches Sara's offer from its date. Sara's offer remains pending, but attempting to accept it fails.
findings.test_needed: Create a pending offer for Sara with single_user_only=false, submit the description-edit payload, and assert its original slot remains linked and accept succeeds.

owner_question.question: When Tom edits only a shift description after offering a date to Sara, what should happen to Sara's offer?
options: Preserve Sara's offer and its original date
Block Tom's edit until outstanding offers are withdrawn
Leave Sara's offer pending but unusable (keep today's behaviour)

findings.title: Automatic escalation can expose shifts earlier than the selected interval.
findings.scenario: Tom in Perth selects automatic escalation from his pharmacy's locum audience to the public board after 24 hours in October. The submitted time has no timezone, so the server interprets it as Sydney time. Sara can see the vacancy three hours earlier than Tom selected.
findings.test_needed: With the client in Australia/Perth and Django in Australia/Sydney during October, assert a 24-hour automatic escalation persists exactly 24 hours after the starting instant.

owner_question.question: When Tom in Perth chooses public visibility after 24 hours, when should Sara gain access?
options: After the full 24 hours Tom selected
At a pharmacy-local time explicitly shown to Tom
At the submitted Sydney time regardless of Tom's timezone (keep today's behaviour)
